Singapore Design Biennale – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Singapore Design Biennale Deadline: Deadline: August 12 Applications are now open for the inaugural Singapore Design Biennale (SDB) 2027 , taking place from 14 May – 20 June 2027 under the theme 1.35°N . Organised by the DesignSingapore Council, the Biennale succeeds Singapore Design Week with an expanded international platform for design, architecture, art and interdisciplinary practice. The theme 1.35°N references Singapore’s geographical latitude and invites designers, architects, artists, researchers, technologists and creative practitioners from around the world to respond to the realities of contemporary life and imagine future possibilities through experimentation, collaboration and innovation. The International Open Call welcomes proposals from independent practitioners, organisations, design festivals and creative brands for exhibitions, installations, workshops, performances, talks, studio visits and other public programmes. Physical projects are preferred, although digital proposals will also be considered where appropriate. Successful programme partners will receive marketing and publicity support through the Singapore Design Biennale. Applicants are responsible for funding, organising and delivering their own projects and securing suitable venues. Successful applicants will be notified by 2 October 2026 . https://sdb.designsingapore.org Info not available biennale@designsingapore.org

items.title: 2026 UMSU Art Prize: Entries Now Open
items.summary: 2026 UMSU Art Prize: Entries Now Open 2026 UMSU Art Prize: Entries Now Open The UMSU Art Prize returns in 2026 to celebrate the legacy of artistic talent and creative labour in Australian student unionism. Entries close Sunday 16 August, midnight. ex-upcoming no-news UMSU and the George Paton Gallery invite submissions from currently enrolled University of Melbourne students working across all visual art and design mediums. The UMSU Art Prize is a biennial award presented by the University of Melbourne Student Union, celebrating the creative practices of currently enrolled University of Melbourne students. Presented at the historic George Paton Gallery, the Prize provides a platform for innovative, critical and experimental artistic practices across visual art and design. Student voices give shape and clarity to the troubles of the present, hope for the future, and lessons of the past — this is your opportunity to add your voice to chorus. ENTRIES CLOSE SUNDAY 16 AUGUST 2026, MIDNIGHT AEST. APPLY NOW VIA OUR ONLINE FORM The UMSU Art Prize offers two awards: $5,000 UMSU Art Prize $1,000 People’s Choice Award Shortlisted artists will have their artworks displayed in the George Paton Gallery for the UMSU Art Prize 2026 exhibition, presented from 17 September to 9 October 2026. The 2026 Judging Panel is comprised of Hannah Presley (Senior Curator, Museums and Collections at University of Melbourne); Brigid Moriarty (Curator, Gertrude); and Sabrina Alday (Arts and Diplomacy Programs Lead, Asialink) The UMSU Art Prize will be announced at the opening event on Friday 18 September, and the People’s Choice Award will be announced on the final day of the exhibition, Friday 9 October. Please note, the Award is non-acquisitive. UMSU ART PRIZE SELECTION CRITERIA The following criteria will be used to assess submissions by the shortlisting panel and guest judges: Artistic Merit: The originality, creativity and technical skill demonstrated in conveying conceptual ideas. Engagement: The effectiveness of the artwork in connecting with a broad audience. Student Powered: The perspective of a student is one that is informed, curious, and analytical. It is important to see these qualities emerge from submitted work, to demonstrate the strength of the student voice. UMSU ART PRIZE SHORTLISTING All submitted artworks will be reviewed by the UMSU Arts and Culture Selection Panel between 3 and 14 August 2026. This shortlisting process is in place to manage submissions effectively, check eligibility, assess the viability of proposed works, and maintain the integrity of the exhibition and award. Only artworks selected through this process will be showcased in the UMSU Art Prize exhibition at the George Paton Gallery and be eligible for an award. Magazine Photography Competition - Celebrating 10 Years 2026 Crikey! Magazine Photography Competition - Celebrating 10 Years In 2026, Australia Zoo proudly celebrates a decade of the Crikey! Magazine Photography Competition – a global platform where photography, storytelling, and conservation unite. Over the past ten years, the competition has brought together photographers and passionate conservationists from around the world, each capturing powerful moments that showcase the extraordinary diversity of life on Earth. Through compelling imagery, these artists help shine a spotlight on the beauty, fragility, and importance of our natural world. Judged by a distinguished panel of acclaimed photographers and naturalists, we invite submissions of outstanding nature, wildlife, and conservation photography. Winning images not only receive prestigious prizes but are also honoured through exhibitions across Australia, allowing thousands of visitors to experience these remarkable works firsthand. Now marking its 10th anniversary, the Crikey! Magazine Photography Competition stands as a celebrated showcase of wildlife photography and a powerful voice for conservation. For a decade, it has inspired audiences to look closer, care deeper, and take action to protect the planet we all share. Join us as we commemorate ten years of extraordinary imagery and continue our mission to connect people with nature, one photograph at a time. Entries open on Monday 15 June and close Monday 31 August 2026. Winners announced Friday 9 October 2026. “ In an era of global change, wildlife and habitats are declining at an unprecedented rate, and it has never been more important to protect the natural world. Through the Crikey! Magazine Photography Competition, it is our mission to showcase the wild kingdom and encourage others to preserve it. " —Robert Irwin Crikey! Cover The winning image will be awarded the cover on the 2026 Summer issue of Crikey! Magazine. To be successful, the image must be portrait orientated with space for the magazine’s title. Entries should be of an animal or the natural world, and compelling as a cover. ENTER NOW! The Natural World A category to celebrate and showcase the beauty of the natural world and thus the need to protect it. Images submitted can showcase wildlife and wild places from anywhere on earth, and depict exciting new perspectives on our complex ecosystems. It is through these images, that we can raise awareness and advocate for the conservation of our precious biodiversity. Images may be landscape or portrait orientated. ENTER NOW! Artists are invited to interpret the building, its architecture, its history, or the broader ideas of labour, community, activism and collective power. Selected works will be exhibited during the Melbourne Fringe Festival at Paddy’s Gallery within Trades Hall. $5,000 Winner’s Prize (Acquisitive) Winning artwork acquired into the Victorian Trades Hall collection. $750 Artist Fee paid to each exhibiting finalist to support production and loan of their artwork. items.summary: 2026 sculpture prize entry form | Art Farm Birchs Bay top of page 2025 winner Alice RG, Play Wariors 2026 SCULPTURE PRIZE This year, in our twentieth year, we are waiving the entry fee as our birthday gift to you!​ ​ Entries close 1 September 2026 at midnight ​ ​ Prizes: $4,000 Major Sculpture Prize $3,000 Kingborough Council Acquisition Prize $3,000 Art Farm Birchs Bay & Five Bob Acquisition Prize $500 People's Choice Award ​ 2026 Guidelines 2026 judges Patrick Hall With an art practice now spanning several decades, Patrick has firmly established a reputation for uniquely intricate and idiosyncratic works. Patrick's ability to cross and often combine seemingly disparate art genres sees a distinct and elegant collision of beautifully fabricated imaginings with prose poetry, cabinetry, lighting and sound recordings. These often emotive pieces are rich in story-telling, sometimes autobiographical, sometimes not. Patrick is represented in public and private collections including the Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery, Hobart; the Museum of Old and New Art [MONA], Berriedale; the Power House Museum, Sydney and the National Gallery of Australia, Canberra. Bob Brown Bob Brown is an Australian former politician, medical doctor, artist, writer, and environmentalist. Bob's most recent book is Defiance. Bob is also an avid photographer and has held numerous solo exhibitions throughout Tasmania and on the mainland. After Bob left the Senate in 2012 he set up the Bob Brown Foundation to take peaceful direct action to stop environmental vandalism, to protect Tasmania’s Takayna rainforest, wildlife and Aboriginal heritage and to end native forest logging nationwide. From leading the seven-year campaign to save Tasmania's wild Franklin River from damming, through fifty-years of finding alternatives to humanity's rapid destruction of life on Earth, Bob Brown's credo has always been 'one person, one vote, one value, one planet'. Peter Johnson Peter Johnson’s ceramic works reflect memory and experience of the Australian landscape visible in the remnants of our industrial, suburban and maritime places, memories of daily living on the land and the expansiveness of the rural environment. For over 35 years Peter has maintained an active studio practice including the Jam Factory, Jamboree Clay Workshop and currently at Gaff Studio, Port Adelaide. For many years he lectured in Ceramics and Visual Arts at TAFE Adelaide College of Arts, O’Halloran Hill and Adelaide campuses. He has had artistic residencies in Barcelona, Spain with the Australia Council and Jingdezhen, China with the Helpmann Academy. Peter’s ceramic work has been shown locally, interstate and internationally. items.summary: Deadline: September 5. Exhibit with Incinerator Gallery – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Exhibit with Incinerator Gallery Deadline: Deadline: September 5 Incinerator Gallery is a platform for unique cultural experiences that connect society through art and design. Share a proposal to exhibit at Incinerator in 2027. Established in 2011 in Aberfeldie, near the Mirrangbamurn/Maribyrnong River, Incinerator Gallery encourages social interaction, discovery, knowledge sharing, learning and development. It welcomes communities, art professionals, students and people of all ages with an interest in art, design and architecture. Housed within the iconic Essendon Incinerator, designed by Marion Mahony Griffin and Walter Burley Griffin, the gallery offers a range of distinctive spaces that invite creative response and engagement. The call-out to exhibit in 2027 at Incinerator Gallery presents an opportunity for artists with a connection to the area, Moonee Valley and the wider Kulin Nation, to apply for exhibition opportunities in The Atrium, Main Gallery or Boadle Hall. Applications are welcome from solo artists, curators and collectives. Key themes for the annual program: Circular economy of materials and clever reuse in design Sustainability Connection to Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung place Day/night activations Participatory practice and installation Successful applicants will receive: An artist or curatorial fee to exhibit, based on NAVA rates ($928–$5,555) A 7–12 week exhibition in one of three galleries across the Incinerator complex Curatorial assistance Marketing support A public program development opportunity An official opening alongside other exhibitions For all EOI information, eligibility criteria and how to apply, please visit the website. https://incineratorgallery.com.au/call-for-proposals-awards 0392431750 incinerator@mvcc.vic.gov.au

items.title: Helsinki International Artist Programme (HIAP)
items.summary: Helsinki International Artist Programme (HIAP) | Creative Australia Skip to main content Community arts and cultural development Dance Emerging and experimental arts Literature Multi-art form Music Theatre Visual Arts Open Helsinki International Artist Programme (HIAP) This three-month residency program offers a $15,000 grant, plus time and space for open-ended research and experimentation on Suomenlinna island in Helsinki. Apply now Helsinki International Artist Programme (HIAP) Key dates Applications close: Tuesday 15 September 2026 at 3:00pm (AEST) Notification date: early December 2026 Please note: To apply you must be registered in our application management system a minimum of two business days prior to the closing date Details Eligible artforms: Community arts and cultural development, Dance, Emerging and experimental arts, First Nations arts and culture, Literature, Music, Theatre, Visual arts Location: Suomenlinna Island in Helsinki, Finland Amount: $15,000 Information pack Further information If you would like advice on your application, please contact the International team: international@creative.gov.au Residency dates 12 April – 4 July 2027 16 August – 14 November 2027 Apply now Please note: To apply you must be registered in our application management system a minimum of two business days prior to the closing date. About the opportunity Founded in 1998, HIAP – Helsinki International Artist Programme – is the largest international residency centre in the Nordic and Baltic region. Every year up to 40 artists and arts professionals residing in Finland and abroad are offered a working period at HIAP. With $15,000 in funding, this three-month residency program offers time and space for open-ended research and experimentation, without the requirement to produce finalised work. The HIAP residency venues are located on Suomenlinna island, a UNESCO World Heritage Site located a 15-minute ferry ride away from the centre of Helsinki, and in the Cable Factory cultural complex in Helsinki. The HIAP residency program focuses on visual arts, however, it is open to artists and curators from various disciplines. Collaborating with local and international partner organisations, residencies extend to such creative fields as dance, theatre, literature, and music. The activities are organised predominantly through thematic residency programs that highlight a geographical area or concentrate on a specific contemporary topic or an aspect of artistic practice. The HIAP residency program offers time and support for developing new work in dialogue with the local art scene. The goal is to offer space for experimental, cross-disciplinary art practices and to actively contribute to topical debates within and around the context of art. The HIAP team help the residents with their research as well as practical everyday matters. Residents have access to services such as weekly residency community meetings, facilities and equipment, and the option to take part in the HIAP Open Studios event. This normally takes place towards the end of each residency season and is an opportunity to present work-in-progress to arts professionals and the general public. More information can be found on the Helsinki International Artist Programme website . You can learn more about the studio, accommodation, local area, and travel arrangements by downloading the Information Pack PDF . The HIAP residency is a highly competitive opportunity. Past successful applicants typically demonstrated a clear rationale regarding the relevance of their proposal to the local arts scene and community. We encourage applicants to read through the assessment panel’s general feedback from the previous round and to contact us for advice. items.summary: Acme London Residency | Creative Australia Skip to main content Visual Arts Open Acme London Residency An opportunity to develop your visual arts practice and professional networks over six months at Acme’s East London residency space, the Fire Station in London with a $30,000 grant. Apply now Acme London Residency Key dates Applications close: Tuesday 15 September 2026 at 3:00pm (AEST) Notification date: November 2026 Please note: To apply you must be registered in our application management system a minimum of two business days prior to the closing date. Details Art form: Visual arts (excluding feature film, television or documentary) Location: London, UK Residency dates: 8 March - 27 August 2027 Amount : $30,000 Further information If you would like advice on your application, please contact the International team, at international@creative.gov.au You can learn more about the studio, accommodation, local area, and travel arrangements by downloading the Information Pack PDF . Apply now Please note: To apply you must be registered in our application management system a minimum of two business days prior to the closing date. About this opportunity Through our partnership with Acme, visual arts professionals (including artists, curators, and arts writers) are offered a six-month residency at Acme’s East London Fire Station residency space. Founded in 1972, Acme Studios is a London-based charity that provides affordable studio space and residencies and awards for non-commercial fine artists. Acme supports over 800 individual artists across 8 boroughs in Greater London, offering a wide range of high-quality, long-term, and professionally managed artist studio spaces, including permanent new-build studios. In addition to affordable studio space, Acme operates a Residency & Awards programme which is one of the most supportive and extensive in the UK. Acme’s programme of artist support aims to intervene at pivotal moments in artists’ careers. Working with a range of international and UK-based partners and donors, the programme supports professional development for artists at all stages of their careers through residencies, bursaries, mentoring and exhibition opportunities. Over 800 artists have benefitted from the programme since its foundation in 1987. Acme makes every effort to assist visiting artists with the practical, cultural, and social aspects of their stay. In addition to managing the studio live/workspace, Acme works actively with visiting artists to assist with their networking, practical and research needs and allowing them to develop relationships and focus on their work in a supported environment. Acme staff are available to artists for residency pre-planning, local orientation and for assistance and advice throughout the residency. The overall aim of Acme’s Residencies & Awards Programme is to offer artists a supported environment and real professional development throughout the residency period. As every artist and their needs are different, Acme representatives are flexible about how they work with artists to achieve their goals. During the residency period, Acme provide resident artists with opportunities including: connecting with UK and international artists through Acme’s networks via Acme-organised events including gallery visits and social gatherings bespoke one-to-one studio critiques or mentor meetings with UK-based arts professionals, organised by Acme opportunity to work in collaboration with Acme staff to hold artist talks, or develop or participate in group discussions, critiques or events one-to-one ongoing support and discussion with Acme staff ongoing notifications and invitations to private views, open studios, lectures, and events in London. More information can be found on the Acme website . You can learn more about the studio, accommodation, local area, and travel arrangements by downloading the Information Pack PDF . About the residency The BR Whiting Studio residency is an opportunity for writers to direct their own program of activity and expand their practice and networks. There are three residencies on offer of varying duration: 1 x one month (with $6,500 support), 1 x three months (with $15,000 support), and 1 x six months (with $27,500 support). The Studio is an apartment in the Roman neighbourhood of Trastevere. It was given to Creative Australia by Lorri Whiting, an Australian abstract painter who was embraced by the Italian art scene. She spent many years living in Rome and exhibited in prestigious galleries across Italy, the UK and New York. She established the BR Whiting Studio as a gift to Creative Australia in honour of her late husband, the writer B.R ‘Bertie’ Whiting. The residency was originally established for the benefit of Australian poets and poets are encouraged to apply for the residency. Due to its location, the apartment can become hot in the summer months. Please take this into consideration when selecting your preferred residency period. Rome is a city rich in history, culture and religion. There are many opportunities for a writer to connect with bookshops, literary societies, universities, academics and translators. Residents are encouraged to make contacts prior to the commencement of their residency. Several previous residents have organised readings through universities and institutions such as the Keats Shelley House. You can learn more about the studio, accommodation, local area, and travel arrangements by downloading the Information Pack PDF . The BR Whiting residency is a highly competitive opportunity. Apply now About the opportunity The International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP) supports the creative development of artists and curators, and promotes exchange through residencies and public programs. Housed in a former factory in Brooklyn, with 35 light-filled work studios and two galleries, ISCP is New York’s most comprehensive international visual arts residency program. It was founded in 1994. ISCP organises exhibitions, events and offsite projects, which are free and open to all, sustaining a vibrant community of contemporary art practitioners and diverse audiences. Over 1,250 artists and curators from more than 75 countries, including the United States, have undertaken residencies at ISCP. The International Studio & Curatorial Program’s mission is: to support and enhance the professional development of emerging to mid-career artists and curators from around the world; to introduce New York audiences to exceptional international art practices; to engage communities of Brooklyn and the New York City area through public programs that enrich the appreciation and understanding of contemporary art. The International Program Residency opportunity at ISCP is for 4 months. While in the International Program, all residents are invited to participate in a number of activities in and outside of ISCP such as Visiting Critics, Field Trips, Salons and Open Studios. Please note that the ISCP will provide each resident a private and furnished studio space to work, however accommodation is not provided through this program. This opportunity provides matched funding alongside fundraising capability development through group training, peer-to peer learning and one on one support and advice. Matched funding is provided on a dollar-for-dollar basis for eligible private sector income raised, up to $10,000. The aims of the fund are for artists and artist groups to move beyond one-off or informal fundraising activity and develop consistent, strategic approaches to generating private sector support. Through participation, artists and artist groups will: build on existing private sector fundraising experience refine how they plan and deliver fundraising activity strengthen relationships with supporters increase confidence and independence as fundraisers. For the purposes of this application, an artist group is defined as two or more individuals who work together but do not form a legally constituted organisation. items.title: What if the traditional art exhibition was just the beginning of a work's impact?
items.summary:
Source: Instagram #artgrant
What if the traditional art exhibition was just the beginning of a work's impact?

We are thrilled to announce that applications for the Emerging Artists for Impact Award 2026 are officially open.

At the IAP Foundation, we are bringing talented emerging artists together, distributing $32,000 in awards, and showcasing their work on a global stage during Miami Art Week.

But our ambition goes much further. We are building a model where art generates both professional opportunity for the creator and measurable change for communities:

20 artists. 20 artworks. Our goal: 20 impact projects.
We are working to connect each selected artwork to tangible initiatives across five key areas: 💧 Clean Water 👥 Children & Youth 📖 Education Access 📈 Economic Empowerment 🌱 Environmental & Community Restoration

Turn art into lasting impact. The jury judges the art. Then the art goes to work.

How you can help: If you are an arts educator, curator, or industry professional, please share this opportunity with your network. Sometimes an opportunity only matters if the right person hears about it.

Eligible applicants include current BFA/MFA students and recent graduates (within two years) from accredited U.S. institutions.

🗓️ Applications close: September 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.

Know someone who should see this? Send this post to them or tag them below. 👇

🔗 Apply / learn more: internationalartproject.submittable.com/submit

Celebrating the magazine’s historic 1966 competition that produced the iconic Swan Dollar , entrants are invited to create both the obverse and reverse of a coin featuring the words “AUSTRALIA 2027” and a design of any nature suitable to Australia . Designs may draw inspiration from Australian flora, fauna, landscapes, culture or other themes. Entries may be submitted as a sketch, concept or finished artwork. items.title: *OPEN CALL* Textiel Biënnale 2027 | Koloniale patronen
items.summary:
Source: Instagram #artopencall
*OPEN CALL* Textiel Biënnale 2027 | Koloniale patronen 

Koloniale patronen zijn overal om ons heen; zichtbaar in de kleding die we dragen, de materialen en stoffen die we gebruiken en de handelsroutes die onze wereld hebben gevormd. In motieven, tradities en productieprocessen, maar ook in machtsverhoudingen, herinneringen en identiteiten. 

Voor de Textiel Biënnale 2027 nodigen we (inter)nationale kunstenaars uit om vanuit hun eigen praktijk en perspectief te reflecteren op het thema Koloniale patronen. Je kunt tot 1 oktober 2026, 12.00 uur een voorstel indienen via museumrijswijk.nl. 

De Textiel Biënnale 2027 | Koloniale patronen vindt plaats van 8 juli tot en met 21 november 2027. 

*OPEN CALL* Textile Biennial 2027 | Colonial patterns

Colonial patterns are all around us; visible in the clothing we wear, the materials and fabrics we use, and the trade routes that have shaped our world. In motifs, traditions, and production processes, but also in power relations, memories, and identities.

For the Textile Biennial 2027, we invite (inter)national artists to reflect on the theme of Colonial patterns from the perspective of their own practice and perspective. You can submit a proposal via museumrijswijk.nl until October 1st, 2026, at 12:00 PM.

The Textile Biennial 2027 | Colonial patterns takes place from July 8 to November 21, 2027.

items.title: OPEN CALL FOR ARTISTS
items.summary:
Source: Instagram #artopencall
OPEN CALL FOR ARTISTS

Strange Homes — “Where the familiar becomes uncertain.”

“ Home is often associated with comfort and belonging, but its meaning is neither stable nor universal. It can change across time and circumstance, shaped by where we live, what we remember, and how we understand ourselves in relation to others. Strange Homes explores these shifts, asking how something comes to feel like home, how that feeling can change, and what new meanings emerge when the familiar becomes uncertain.

No single experience defines home. The exhibition welcomes both personal and broader social perspectives, inviting artists to consider how ideas of home are formed, inherited, questioned, or reimagined, and how the familiar can take on different meanings over time. “

Rexhibit Online Gallery invites artists worldwide to submit work for Strange Homes, an international online group exhibition centered on the changing meanings of home.

AWARDS:
Gold Award — Online Solo Exhibition + Featured Interview
Silver Award — Online Solo Exhibition
Bronze Award — Featured Interview
Honorable Mention — Special recognition

Selected artists receive a dedicated exhibition presentation, digital catalog, promotional support, optional artwork inquiry feature, and consideration for future Rexhibit projects.

All mediums are welcome.

SUBMISSION FEE:
$18 for 1–3 works
$20 for 4–8 works

DEADLINE:
October 1, 2026

🔗 View the full guidelines and apply through the link in bio.

Kilgour Prize 2027 – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Kilgour Prize 2027 Deadline: Deadline: October 5 Entries are now open for the Kilgour Prize 2027 , one of Australia’s leading annual awards for figurative and portrait painting . Presented by Newcastle Art Gallery , the non-acquisitive prize awards AUD $50,000 for the most outstanding work selected by the judging panel, with an additional AUD $5,000 People’s Choice Award presented during the finalists’ exhibition. Celebrating its 20th anniversary , the Kilgour Prize was established through the bequest of Newcastle artist Jack Noel Kilgour (1900–1987) and has become a significant platform for both emerging and established figurative painters. Previous recipients include Nicholas Harding , Natasha Walsh , Blak Douglas , Michael Bell and Peter Gardiner . The 2027 judging panel comprises Lauretta Morton OAM , Kelli Cole and Jason Phu . Approximately selected finalist works will be exhibited at Newcastle Art Gallery from April to August 2027. Eligible works must have been completed between 4 October 2025 and 4 October 2026 . Applications are submitted online and require an image upload and entry fee payment. https://newcastleartgallery.nsw.gov.au/kilgour-prize 0249745100 artgallery@ncc.nsw.gov.au

items.summary: Deadline: October 6. Shirley Hannan National Portrait Award – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Shirley Hannan National Portrait Award Deadline: Deadline: October 6 Entries are now open for the Shirley Hannan National Portrait Award 2026 , a biennial $50,000 non-acquisitive award celebrating excellence in realistic portrait painting. Presented by the South East Centre for Contemporary Art (SECCA) , the award is one of Australia’s major portrait prizes and is distinguished by its commitment to realism. Eligible works must depict a living person known to the artist , who is aware of and has participated in the portrait-making process. Abstraction is not permitted. The 2026 award introduces several initiatives to better support artists, including a reduced entry fee, an artist loan fee for finalists and a contribution towards artwork freight costs. Previous recipients include Lucy Culliton , Shaun Gladwell and Sally Robinson . The 2026 judging panel will be announced by SECCA. items.summary: Deadline: October 7. Earth Partner Prize 2026 – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Earth Partner Prize 2026 Deadline: Deadline: October 7 The Earth Partner Prize 2026 is now open for submissions, inviting artists and creatives aged 14–30 from around the world to respond to the urgent challenges of climate change, ecological justice and environmental action. Open to all nationalities, backgrounds and creative disciplines, the prize welcomes submissions across a broad range of mediums including photography, film, sculpture, performance, writing, music, fashion, coding, digital art, new media, app development and social media projects. The initiative aims to amplify the voices of younger generations whose futures will be shaped by today’s environmental decisions. Presented in collaboration with the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and Re:wild, the prize offers emerging creatives the opportunity to have their work showcased internationally and viewed by environmental leaders, curators and cultural organisations. Eight finalists will receive cash prizes of $10,000, $5,000 or $2,000, while an additional twenty artists will receive Honourable Mentions selected by an internationally recognised jury. A special Impact Award will also be presented. The 2026 jury includes Hans Ulrich Obrist, Ferdinando Verderi, Shaway Yeh, Musonda Mumba, Derrick O. Boateng, Robin D. Moore, Giovanni Testino, Marcela Villafaña and Marina Testino. Selected works will be featured on Earth Partner and Art Partner platforms, reaching global audiences and continuing the prize’s history of exhibitions at major venues including the United Nations Headquarters, Fotografiska Shanghai and Photo London. items.title: Impact Investment Readiness Program
items.summary: Impact Investment Readiness Program | Creative Australia Skip to main content Capability development Multi-art form Opening Soon Impact Investment Readiness Program Build a stronger, more sustainable organisation. Impact Investment Readiness Program Stage 1 Key Dates Online information session: to be announced Expression of Interest (EOI) opens: Monday 12 October 2026 EOI closes : Friday 30 October 2026, 3pm AEDT Notification of outcomes for EOI and invitation to Stage 2: by 13 November 2026 Stage 2 Key Dates Full Applications (invitation only): by Friday 20 November 2026 Notification of Stage 2 outcomes : December 2027 Program commences : 15 February 2027 Program ends : 15 May 2027 Contact If you have a question about eligibility, or need help with your application, please email . Social Enterprise Finance Australia (Sefa) Find out more about Sefa, our delivery partner, here . About the program The Impact Investment Readiness Program is being delivered in partnership between Creative Australia and Social Enterprise Finance Australia (Sefa). It supports creative and cultural organisations to strengthen their foundations, build long-term sustainability and explore impact investment as a potential source of capital. Arts organisations make a vital contribution to Australia’s cultural, social and economic life. Many, however, face challenges securing the capital needed to invest in growth and future sustainability. Impact investing offers an alternative pathway that seeks both measurable social, cultural or environmental impact and financial returns. Through the program, organisations will strengthen their business capability, better understand and articulate their impact, use evidence to support decision-making, and build confidence in planning for their future. Image: The Hum feat. artists of The Australian Ballet and artists of Australian Dance Theatre. Photo: Daniel Boud Program overview Expand all Collapse all Why does impact investing readiness matter? Investment readiness is more than accessing finance. Investment readiness means you can clearly articulate your impact in front of funders, have stronger business, governance and financial management in place and a clear plan to future proof your organisation. What you will learn and apply Through the program, participants will build practical knowledge, skills and tools to strengthen organisational sustainability, impact and readiness for future growth. You will learn how to: articulate, measure and communicate the impact of your work through a theory of change and impact measurement framework identify opportunities for income stream diversification and what needs to be in place to make this happen strengthen business planning for organisational sustainability and growth develop a growth/sustainability strategy and implementation plan aligned with your mission and impact identify and assess future funding options best suited to you, including impact investment. These skills can help organisations to: demonstrate impact to attract new partners, supporters, collaborators improve strategic planning and decision-making strengthen organisational sustainability and resilience prepare and pursue future growth opportunities. While the program supports organisations to build investment readiness, the skills, tools and frameworks developed will benefit participants regardless of whether impact investment is ultimately the right pathway for their organisation. What is involved The Impact Investment Readiness Program is delivered online over 14 weeks and combines practical learning, expert guidance and peer engagement to help organisations learn and apply new skills directly to their work. Participants will receive: self-paced online learning modules practical tools and templates online group sessions to exchange learnings with other peer organisations online individual coaching support to enhance application (Stream 1 participants only). The program will support up to 20 organisations

items.summary: National Songwriting and Recording in Schools Stimulus | Creative Australia Skip to main content Music Open National Songwriting and Recording in Schools Stimulus Up to $100,000 in matched funding to support high-quality, inclusive contemporary songwriting and recording programs for primary, secondary and tertiary students in schools, TAFEs, universities and other music academies across Australia. Apply now National Songwriting and Recording in Schools Stimulus Key dates Applications close Tuesday 13 October 2026 at 3pm AEDT Activity must start from 27 January 2027 and be completed by 31 December 2027 Amount Between $5,000 & $100,000 in matched funding. Contact If you need advice about eligibility and the program, contact Music Australia . If you need advice on how to register in our system, contact an Artists Services Officer . Apply now You must be registered in our Application Management System to apply for a grant. Registrations take up to two business days to process. NOTE: You will not be able to apply to the Tuesday 13 October 2026 closing date unless you register before 10am AEDT on Monday 12 October 2026. Registrations received after this time will not be processed until Wednesday 14 October. About the program The National Songwriting and Recording in Schools Stimulus (NSRSS) provides targeted matched funding to support high quality, inclusive songwriting and recording programs in schools, TAFEs, universities and other music academies across Australia. The program is for students/learners, educators and their partners. Program priorities Priority will be given to activities that: strengthen access to songwriting and recording opportunities for students, including those in regional, remote, outer suburban or under-served communities (the Accessibilty/Remoteness Index of Australia (ARIA) helps determine if your location is metropolitan, regional, remote or very remote – you can download the ARIA Code list from our website ). promote inclusive and equitable participation are First Nations-led or demonstrate strong First Nations partnership and cultural integrity build connections between learning and pathways or next step opportunities demonstrate strong local partnership and community benefit create sustainable or repeatable models rather than one-off activity increase teacher, mentor and provider capability strengthen contemporary music practice, including collaboration and creative development create teaching, mentoring or co-delivery opportunities for emerging or working composers, songwriters, producers and engineers, with priority given to those based locally to the delivery area. Please read the following guidelines for further information. If you need advice about applying contact Music Australia . Image: Birdland, Mount Lawley High School Expand all Collapse all Eligibility Who can apply government primary and secondary schools Catholic and independent primary and secondary schools school clusters or regional school consortia private music academies specialist music providers TAFEs Australian universities community conservatoria consortia including at least one educational institution Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) local councils music charities and foundations. The applying organisation must be located in Australia, majority Australian owned, and have been operating for a minimum of two years. The proposed activity must meet the Music Australia Council’s agreed definition of contemporary music, as follows: “Australian contemporary music is any genre or subgenre of music currently composed, written, produced by Australians and licensed, recorded, presented, and distributed through commercial and non-commercial activity. ANAT: Synapse Residency Program 2027 – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu ANAT: Synapse Residency Program 2027 Deadline: Deadline: October 14 Applications are now open for the 2027 ANAT Synapse Residency Program , supporting Australian artists to undertake a creative research residency in partnership with a leading Australian research organisation. The program brings together artists and researchers to explore the intersections of art, science and technology through collaborative experimentation. Rather than focusing on a predetermined outcome, the residency encourages the development of new ideas, knowledge and creative processes that benefit both artistic and scientific fields. One residency will be awarded in 2027, with the successful artist completing a 16-week full-time residency (or part-time equivalent). Artists will receive a fee plus superannuation, with additional project expenses supported where required. items.summary: Biennale Delegates Program 2026 | Creative Australia Skip to main content Visual Arts Closed Biennale Delegates Program 2026 Creative Australia’s Biennale Delegates Program is a professional development opportunity for individuals working in the visual arts sector (producers, technicians, writers, curators, artists, project managers) who are living in Australia. Biennale Delegates Program 2026 Key dates Applications closed Notification: late-May 2026 Program dates May – October 2026 Group Session 1: late-May (online introduction) Sydney: 10 – 14 June - Biennale of Sydney (face-to-face) Group Session 2: mid-July (online workshop) Group Session 3: mid-August (online workshop) Venice: 17 – 27 September - Venice Biennale (face-to-face) Closing: 31 October (report due) Contact If you need advice about applying, contact us . Phone: 02 9215 9000 Toll-free: 1800 226 912 NRS: 1800 555 677 | Visit the NRS Email: venice@creative.gov.au or enquiries@creative.gov.au . About the program Creative Australia’s Biennale Delegates Program is a professional development opportunity for individuals working in the visual arts sector (producers, technicians, writers, curators, artists, project managers) who are living in Australia. The program will facilitate an exchange of ideas, catalyse new perspectives, and support the seeding of future projects and collaborations. In 2026, the total intake for the program will be eight (8) individuals, one (1) representative from each State and Territory from across Australia. This program is for individuals: who are early career, within five to ten years of practice or experience as a creative practitioner interested in applying learnings from participation in the program to their practice wanting to develop or expand their national and global international networks wanting to explore shared global challenges to benefit Australian creative practice interested in identifying future international projects or collaborations from NSW, who live in Western Sydney. Create NSW defines Western Sydney as the thirteen local government areas of Blacktown City, Blue Mountains City, Camden Council, Campbelltown City, The City of Canterbury Bankstown, Cumberland Council, Fairfield City, Hawkesbury City, Liverpool City, The City of Parramatta, Penrith City, The Hills Shire, and Wollondilly Shire. The Biennale Delegates Program is a co-investment initiative with Create NSW, artsACT, Arts Tasmania, Arts Queensland, Create SA, Arts NT, and WA Government, and is philanthropically supported by the Cross Family Foundation. Program format In 2026, the Biennale Delegates Program returns as a distinctive initiative fostering creative exchange, critical dialogue, and professional development across global art platforms. Offering access to Australian and international events – including the Biennale of Sydney and Venice Biennale – the program positions delegates at the forefront of contemporary visual arts discourse. Developed and delivered by Creative Australia in a hybrid format, participants will shape their experience through curated workshops, mentorship with sector leaders, and collaborative learning. This immersive approach deepens understanding of curatorial practice, cultural mediation, audience engagement, and future-facing strategies shaping the arts. Delegates will need to commit to 14 days of in-person engagement in June and September, plus international travel. Support Successful applicants will receive a grant of AUD $4,750 to support their participation, professional development opportunities and outcomes. This grant includes: $400 allowance for the Sydney intensive to cover additional meals, airport transfer and incidentals. $850 allowance for the Venice, Italy intensive to cover additional meals, airport transfer and incidentals. items.summary: Deadline: November 17. John Ruskin Prize: Not for Present Delight – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu John Ruskin Prize: Not for Present Delight Deadline: Deadline: November 17 The John Ruskin Prize returns for its ninth year, inviting artists, designers and makers from anywhere in the world to submit work responding to the theme Not for Present Delight . Taking its title from the writings of John Ruskin, this year’s theme asks whether art must serve a purpose beyond itself, or whether it can exist simply for pleasure. It also considers what it means to create with an awareness of consequence in a time defined by environmental urgency and social inequality. The prize is open to amateur and professional artists, designers and makers working across any 2D or 3D medium, including drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, photography, textiles, animation, digital art, performance, installation and mixed media. Elaine Bermingham National Watercolour Prize in Landscape Painting – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Elaine Bermingham National Watercolour Prize in Landscape Painting Deadline: Deadline: November 30 The Elaine Bermingham National Watercolour Prize in Landscape Painting is a triennial award presented by Griffith University’s Queensland College of Art and Design, celebrating excellence and innovation in watercolour. The prize is open to Australian artists over the age of 18. The overall winner will receive a $20,000 non-acquisitive cash prize , generously donated by Elaine Bermingham. For the purposes of the prize, landscape is defined broadly as any form of land or environment. Peopled landscapes, seascapes, urbanised environments and rural habitats are all eligible. Works do not need to be representational, with innovative and abstracted approaches to watercolour welcomed. Finalists will be selected for an exhibition at QCAD Galleries at Griffith University’s Brisbane City Campus, South Bank. The 2026 principal judge is Alison Kubler , Editor in Chief of VAULT magazine, a member of the Queensland Art Gallery Board of Trustees and a curator with more than 30 years’ experience across Australian museums, galleries and major public art commissions. The pre-selection panel comprises Professor Julie Fragar, Dr Laini Burton and Associate Professor Natalya Hughes . https://www.griffith.edu.au/arts-education-law/queensland-college-art-design/the-elaine-bermingham-prize 61737356106 berminghamprize@griffith.edu.au

items.title: Submissions Are Now Open | Works On Paper 2027
items.summary:
Deadline: 12 noon
Source: Instagram #artopencall
SUBMISSIONS ARE NOW OPEN | WORKS ON PAPER 2027

Green & Stone is delighted to announce the sixth edition of Works on Paper, our annual international open call and exhibition celebrating work made on, or with, paper.
Works on Paper 2027 will be particularly special. Opening in January, it will be the first exhibition of Green & Stone’s centenary year, beginning our celebration of 100 years since Green & Stone was founded in Chelsea in 1927.

We are inviting artists to submit work across drawing, watercolour, printmaking, collage, illustration, book arts, mixed media and experimental approaches to paper. We welcome submissions from artists at every stage of their practice, from emerging artists to established names.

Selected works will be exhibited at The Gallery at Green & Stone in London from 11 January – 3 February 2027, alongside a programme of events celebrating paper, materials and making.

Key dates
Submissions close: 12 noon, Wednesday 25 November 2026 Results announced: Wednesday 2 December 2026 Exhibition: 11 January – 3 February 2027 Private View: Tuesday 12 January 2027

Full submission details, eligibility, entry fees and terms can be found via the link in our bio.

Join us for this very special anniversary exhibition. We cannot wait to see what you have been making.

This opportunity includes two gallery spaces: the Angela Robarts-Bird (ARB) Gallery, a white box exhibition space, and the James McCaughey Foyer Gallery, a high-traffic, multi-use space ideal for group exhibitions. Gasworks welcomes multidisciplinary proposals from emerging to established artists, including painting, sculpture, video, installation, performance, photography, and mixed media. Applications are open to both solo artists and groups. Artists with experimental practices are encouraged to apply, and enquiries are welcomed prior to submission. While Gasworks is based in Melbourne, Brisbane artists are eligible to apply. Located in Albert Park, Gasworks Arts Park is a major cultural precinct combining galleries, theatres, studios, and parklands, engaging over 100,000 visitors annually. items.title: Five Sisters Funded Artist Residency
items.summary: Deadline: April 20. Five Sisters Funded Artist Residency – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Five Sisters Funded Artist Residency Deadline: Deadline: April 20 The Five Sisters Funded Artist Residency is a unique opportunity offered by Edenhope Artist Residency (EAR), supporting artists to immerse themselves in a quiet regional environment in western Victoria. Funded by the descendants of David and Mary Burns and their five daughters—Teenie, Belle, Jean, Nellie and Jessie—the residency honours deep family connections to Edenhope and aims to foster new creative relationships between artists and the local community. This funded residency covers the full residency fee and includes a $500 stipend, providing time, space, and support for artists to focus on their practice. items.title: Artists Exchange: Making Work
items.summary: Deadline: June 5. Artists Exchange: Making Work – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Artists Exchange: Making Work Deadline: Deadline: June 5 Artists Exchange: Making Work is a month-long online professional development program designed for emerging and early career artists across regional and remote Queensland. The program offers a supportive and welcoming environment where artists can connect, share current work, and participate in constructive peer critique sessions. Across four weekly online sessions, participants will take part in ‘show and tell’ style discussions focused on artwork feedback, creative development, and building confidence within a community of peers. Sessions are intentionally small, with up to eight artists per group. The program will be facilitated by Dr Holly Arden (Flying Arts; former Director of Townsville City Galleries) and Alison McDonald, a Gurambilbarra/Townsville-based artist and recipient of the 2025 Art for Life Award at the Queensland Regional Art Awards. Participants can choose between a morning or afternoon session running across the following Mondays: July 6 July 13 July 20 July 27, 2026 Morning sessions run from 10:00am – 11:15am, while afternoon sessions run from 3:30pm – 4:45pm. The program is suitable for artists aged 18+ working across all media who are open to giving and receiving thoughtful and constructive feedback. Applications close Friday June 5, 2026 at 4:00pm. Spaces are limited and interested artists are encouraged to apply early. https://flyingarts.org.au 61732161322 development@flyingarts.org.au

items.title: Khoj International Residency
items.summary: Deadline: June 7. Khoj International Residency – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Khoj International Residency Deadline: Deadline: June 7 Khoj International Artists’ Association has announced the open call for its International Residency, taking place from 3 August to 16 September 2026 at Khoj Studios in New Delhi, India. This six-week onsite residency invites artists working across disciplines to explore the intersections of mental health, distress, and the ways pain—physical, psychological, and historical—shapes both individuals and societies. Applicants are encouraged to examine how suffering is distributed across race, caste, class, gender, and geography, and how people and communities navigate, resist, and reclaim vitality in the face of war, colonial legacies, and systemic inequality. The residency also welcomes projects that engage with clinical and everyday experiences, myth and ritual, oral histories, ancestral knowledge, and emerging technologies. By bringing together artists and scholars from India and the United Kingdom, the program aims to expand conversations around mental health and contemporary life-worlds. Presented in collaboration with the Centre for Anthropology and Mental Health Research in Action (CAMHRA) at SOAS University of London, the residency is open to Indian and international artists. One UK-based artist will be supported directly by CAMHRA. Selected artists will receive travel to and from Delhi, a per diem, and a production budget. https://khojstudios.org Info not available applications@khojstudios.org

items.summary: Australian Photography Awards FAQ Australian photography awards 2026 ENTER NOW Image by Aletheia Casey ENTRIES OPEN Until June 15th, 2026 PRIZE POOL A$17,000 prize pool from Nikon Australia, HC Pro, Tecart, and The Brownbill Effect + Exhibition Opportunities Read More ENTRY FEE $30AUD per submission Now in its TENTH edition, APA 2026 is CELEBRATING A DECADE of AustraliaN photography The Australian Photography Awards returns for its 10th edition in 2026, celebrating the strength and diversity of photographic practice across the country. This year, the awards move to a single Open Category, inviting photographers to submit work across all genres from portraiture and landscape to documentary, wildlife, experimental, and contemporary practices. Rather than dividing photography into separate categories, the awards recognise that today’s image-making often moves fluidly across styles and disciplines. The judging committee will select five winning images from the pool of entries that best represent where Australian photography is at in 2026. Students currently enrolled in a recognised course may also opt into a Student Category at no additional cost when submitting a paid entry. The awards remain committed to photography grounded in original image capture. While digital editing is permitted, AI-generated imagery is not accepted, and any AI-assisted editing must be disclosed during the entry process. APA Exhibition & Event Program Finalists and shortlisted artists will be exhibited through print and projection as part of an exhibition program. Taking place in Naarm/Melbourne during July 2026. The APA Exhibition & Event Program will bring together artists and photographers from across Australia to share their work, make connections and celebrate photography. Introducing the 2026 Committee This year we’ve refined our approach, bringing together a focused committee to guide the award’s direction. With one category and multiple prizes, this group will work collaboratively to recognise the most compelling work submitted, drawing on the insight of leading Australian image makers, curators and educators who will consider this year’s entrants and champion standout photography. Awarded every three years, the Prize recognises outstanding, original painting in oil or watercolour (including gouache). In recognition of this important contribution, the NSW Government has introduced the Championing NSW Music Policy , which encourages government agencies to prioritise NSW music in their campaigns, initiatives and events. To help government agencies build their knowledge of the talent our state has to offer, Sound NSW is conducting a call out for NSW artists/acts and songwriters to join a database of NSW music professionals, called the Championing NSW Music database. The database will act as a resource to help government agencies discover NSW talent for consideration for use. This might include live performances at events, bespoke commissions for advertising campaigns, synchronisation opportunities for video/social media content, or the inclusion of music in playlists for events. If you are a NSW artist/act or songwriter (or represent one), and you would like to be included in the Championing NSW Music database, please fill out the form below . How to get involved Complete the submission form here . Please note that submitting your details to this database does not guarantee future work from the NSW Government. However, it will increase the opportunity to be contacted for NSW Government projects, initiatives and events. For more information on the Championing NSW Music database including how your information will be used, please visit the Frequently Asked Questions . Founded on the belief that art is inherently nomadic—crossing borders, cultures, and contexts—the prize seeks to recognise artists whose work embodies themes of movement, displacement, travel, and belonging. For its 2026 edition, the Nomad Art Prize will take place in Lisbon, Portugal. Drawing inspiration from the city’s layered history, maritime heritage, and vibrant contemporary culture, the program invites artists from around the world to respond to the tensions between roots and movement through their creative practice. Open to artists aged 16 and over from all nationalities, the prize welcomes submissions of one to three artworks. Applications will be reviewed by an international jury of curators, who will select eight artists to participate in the program. Selected artists will each receive a €1,000 cash prize and be invited to attend a one-week creative residency in Lisbon, with travel and accommodation included. The residency will culminate in an exhibition at the renowned LX Factory in October 2026. Artists retain full ownership and copyright of their submitted works. https://nomadartprize.com Info not available hello@nomadartprize.com

items.summary: trenarren HOUSE Artist Residency – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu trenarren HOUSE Artist Residency Deadline: Applications are open for the 2025/2026 trenarren HOUSE Residency Season , inviting artists from all creative disciplines to immerse themselves in a unique rural residency centred on the theme Community . Located on the coast of Cornwall, United Kingdom , trenarren HOUSE is a multidisciplinary artist-run residency where creativity and wellbeing intersect. Artists are encouraged to dedicate focused time to their practice while living alongside a small community of fellow creatives in a supportive environment inspired by nature, collaboration and self-directed exploration. Residencies are available from one to six months , welcoming practitioners working across visual art, sculpture, ceramics, photography, performance, film, music, writing, architecture, curatorial practice and interdisciplinary arts. Residents receive a private room, shared studio facilities, fresh locally sourced meals, access to creative spaces including painting and writing studios, a sound recording suite, yoga studio, musical instruments, woodland gardens and wellness activities including yoga, sauna, sea swims and nature walks. Participation in workshops and community activities is entirely optional, allowing artists to shape their own residency experience. Set within over two acres of woodland and just a short walk from the beach, trenarren HOUSE offers an intimate environment for artists seeking time, connection and creative renewal. https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScG4lmU573q-JWvhKUTbqoX-fAViOfOPvkbnHoHN2SheytuOQ/viewform 4407779111151 Info not available

items.title: 🎨 OPEN CALL — HARMONY 🎨
items.summary:
Source: Instagram #artopencall
🎨 OPEN CALL — HARMONY 🎨

Indra Gallery | 31st October

What does harmony mean to you?

Harmony can be found in many forms — in the balance between light and shadow, colour and form, movement and stillness. It can exist between people, cultures, nature, or within ourselves.

For this exhibition, we invite artists to explore the many faces of Harmony:

🌿 Harmony with Nature — our relationship with the natural world, cycles, landscapes, and living things.

🤝 Harmony Between People — connection, community, empathy, collaboration, and the beauty of coexistence.

🌓 Inner Harmony — balance within ourselves, between thought and emotion, chaos and calm, solitude and connection.

🎨 Harmony in Art — colour, composition, texture, rhythm, contrast, and the visual relationships that bring an artwork together.

⚡ Harmony in Contrast — the idea that opposing elements can coexist: light and dark, softness and strength, order and chaos.

🌍 Cultural Harmony — different traditions, identities, histories, and perspectives coming together without losing their individuality.

🎶 Harmony & Rhythm — repetition, movement, sound, pattern, and the invisible rhythms that shape our lives.

✨ Harmony in the Everyday — finding beauty and balance in ordinary moments, spaces, relationships, and experiences.

We welcome artists working across painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, mixed media, textiles, digital art, and other visual practices to interpret the theme in their own way.

items.summary:

Open Call | What Remains? International Juried Exhibition 

Asian Art Contemporary™ invites submissions for the virtual exhibition What Remains?, a showcase exploring what persists after moments, places, relationships, and ways of life have changed or disappeared. Artists Jennifer Ling Datchuk jenniferlingdatchuk, Kazuhito Kawai kazuhitokawai, and Yeonsu Ju yeonsuju, together with Ben Hsiao s1101_km, Co-Founder and Director of Artemin Gallery artemin.gallery, have been invited as jurors for this open call. Bringing perspectives across artistic and institutional practices, their selections will reflect the exhibition’s interest in diverse approaches to memory, transformation, and the traces that endure over time. What Remains seeks works that consider remnants not simply as evidence of what has been lost, but as active forms through which experiences can be revisited, reinterpreted, and given new meaning.

Who Can Apply
▪️Open to Asian artists worldwide, at all career stages.
▪️All traditional and digital media are welcome, including painting, sculpture, photography, video, mixed media, and more.
▪️Submitted work must be original, and artists are responsible for copyright compliance.

Selected Artist Benefits
▪️Virtual Exhibition: Work presented in a curated online exhibition.
▪️Artist Interview: Complimentary interview highlighting each artist’s practice and story.
▪️Social Media Promotion: Promotion through our official Instagram account.

items.title: 90 Sekunden. So viel Zeit hat eine Jurymappe im Schnitt beim ersten Durchgang.
items.summary:
Source: Instagram #artgrant
90 Sekunden. So viel Zeit hat eine Jurymappe im Schnitt beim ersten Durchgang.
Was in dieser Zeit passiert:
Das erste Bild entscheidet, ob überhaupt weitergeblättert wird - es trägt mehr Gewicht als jedes andere.
Konsistenz der Werkgruppe zählt mehr als ein einzelnes starkes Bild dazwischen.
Rechtschreibfehler im Anschreiben fallen in der ersten Minute auf und bleiben im Kopf.
Unklare Struktur kostet Zeit, die die Jury nicht hat - und Zeit, die sie nicht gibt.
Das heißt nicht: alles muss perfekt sein. Es heißt: die ersten Eindrücke verdienen die meiste Sorgfalt.
Mehr im Verzeichnis - Link in Bio

items.title: Steve Buccellato has chosen the winners of this year's art prize, and we'd like to start the announc
items.summary:
Source: Instagram #artprize
Steve Buccellato has chosen the winners of this year's art prize, and we'd like to start the announcements with the artists who didn't make the top prizes, but Steve felt deserved an acknowledgement.

Our next shout out goes to Frank Freire frankfreireffs , congrats Frank! You made Steve's job really difficult with your terrific work.

From Steve:

"Wow, this was a tough assignment! The volume of entries was intimidating enough, but comparing works from such varied genres, styles and mediums was quite a challenge. It almost doesn’t seem fair to compare some of the more divergent works with one another!

That being said, I approached the task by deciding on some universal criteria that could apply to all styles and genres, so I could judge each on their own merits. Those criteria included elements of craft, such as composition, anatomy, color theory, but also more intangible or subjective criteria like “overall feels,” individuality, and storytelling– which, to me, is one of the most important elements of a successful illustration."

Submissions are open!

The Brooklyn Review will be accepting fiction, poetry, essays, and visual art from September 1 through September 30. 

-General Guidelines-
The Brooklyn Review accepts submissions during our two annual reading periods: February 1 – 28th and September 1 – 30th.

We accept only previously unpublished submissions, and we do not accept submissions by email; please submit only via our Submittable page. For fiction, standard manuscript format is preferred.

Simultaneous submissions are allowed, but we ask that you notify us right away if a piece is accepted for publication elsewhere. The editorial staff also reserves the right to edit accepted work in collaboration with the author or artist. Work created using generative AI will not be considered for publication. Due to the volume of work we receive we unfortunately cannot provide feedback on declined submissions.

We’re excited to read and see what you’ve been working on.

Offering $500–$1,000 in flexible, small-scale funding to artists, curators, institutions and nonprofits, the program backs the bold, the curious, and the not-yet-proven, helping promising work find its way into the world.

From exhibitions and publications to research, public programs, special initiatives, and creative experiments, these grants are designed to support ideas that can make a meaningful impact with modest support.

Grants are awarded on a limited and discretionary basis. There is no open application process. Recipients are identified through the Foundation’s ongoing engagement with individuals and organizations, through direct inquiry, or, at the Foundation’s discretion, by invitation to submit a proposal.

items.title: // Issue 75 - Clay Every Which Way //
items.summary:
Source: Instagram #artopencall
// Issue 75 - Clay Every Which Way //

Clay is one of humanity's oldest creative companions. It records fingerprints, holds memory, cracks under pressure, hardens through fire, and can return to the earth. It exists somewhere between permanence and impermanence, control and chance, utility and expression... 

For this issue of HAUS-A-REST, we invited artists to explore Clay Every Which Way. We are interested in clay beyond the pot, beyond tradition, beyond expectation.

We selected work that embraces ceramics, sculpture, installation or functional objects.

The clay appears only as an idea, a metaphor for transformation, identity, labour, geology, archaeology, ritual, play, memory, or the body itself.

The work spans the use of unfired clay, clay slips, earth pigments, digital clay simulation, or explores landscapes where clay is found.

This issue also explores repetition, touch, repair, fragility, resilience, or the relationship between maker and material.

Submissions are now open for Issue 4 of VERMEER Magazine.

For every issue, our FOCUS section introduces selected contemporary realist artists through one outstanding work. Artists can be selected for one of two formats: FOCUS, a two-page feature dedicated to one artist with an artwork and editorial texts about the work and artist, or FOCUS compact, where several selected artists are presented together across two pages with one artwork and a concise accompanying text each. Both formats are selected through the same open call.

To apply, send 3–5 high-resolution images of different works to editorial@vermeer-magazine.com. Please include captions for each work (title, year, size and technique), your full name and contact details, website, a text about the submitted artwork (max. 200 words) and a text about yourself as an artist (max. 200 words). One artwork will be selected for publication.

The submission fee is 25 CHF (approx. 24 GBP / 27 EUR / 32 USD; the daily exchange rate applies) and can be paid via PayPal to lichtschlag@freiheitsfunken.info. 🎤 thorn.haze is a multi-instrument singer/songwriter known for blending indie, rock, alternative and blues. 

His breakthrough came in 2023, when he launched a year-long project to write and record a new song every day in remote locations. Thorn received a Koch Cultural Trust grant in 2026 and is using it to expand his opportunities to share his music by going on tour. “I expected a no, but here I am going on tour,” he said. “If it could happen to me, it could happen to you.” 

If you’re an aspiring Kansas musician or artist, apply for a Koch Cultural Trust grant before October 1 and get help jumpstarting your next great idea. Visit the link in our bio for eligibility details and to apply.

items.title: Puddle gallery is launching an open call for its Fall 2026 show called I thought California would be
items.summary:
Source: Instagram #artopencall
Puddle gallery is launching an open call for its Fall 2026 show called I thought California would be different ! It is scheduled to open on November 7 in Koreatown 🏖️

Open call deadline is Sunday, October 11 at 11:59 pm

Application link in the bio 🏝️

I thought California Would Be Different takes its title from Raymond Pettibon’s No Title (I Thought California Would Be Different) and uses the phrase as a starting point rather than a conclusion. The exhibition considers the distance between an imagined California and the one we actually encounter: a place so heavily pictured in advance through ideas of sunlight, freedom, reinvention, beauty, glamour, success and failure that arriving here can feel like meeting something you already know. 

We invite work that responds to what happens when those expectations shift — through disappointment or disillusionment, but also through affection, surprise, belonging, or the discovery that California is stranger, richer, or better than anticipated. The prompt can be approached literally, personally, politically, humorously, or abstractly; we are interested in the many ways a real place exceeds, contradicts, fulfills, or transforms the version of it we carried with us.

Eine Residency ist selten kostenlos - auch wenn 'gefördert' draufsteht.
Was oft nicht im Angebot steckt:
Anreisekosten - viele Programme decken nur Aufenthalt und Arbeitsraum, nicht den Flug oder Zug dorthin.
Verpflegung vor Ort ist oft teurer als zuhause kalkuliert, besonders in touristischen Regionen.
Während des Aufenthalts fällt reguläres Einkommen aus zuhause weg - das rechnet kaum jemand vorher durch.
Materialkosten vor Ort sind selten im Stipendium enthalten, auch wenn 'Arbeitsraum gestellt' klingt wie alles inklusive.
Vor Zusage genau nachfragen, was konkret gedeckt ist - nicht nach der Ankunft überrascht werden.
Speichern für die nächste Bewerbung.

Save. Beim nächsten Antrag dankst du dir selbst.

Welcher Satz trifft? Sag's in den Kommentaren.
